title: Oath of Claws
logline: A hunted shapeshifter assassin and the warden she was sold to kill raid her guild for the ledger that owns every odiyan, and the first contract she translates names her as the lookout at his sister's murder.
central_question: Can they steal the guild's ledger without becoming its new masters?

heroine_belief.opening: What the guild made me do isn't mine to answer for.
heroine_belief.changed: I owe repair even for what I was made to do.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Rain
chapters.goal: Make a plan to take the ledger before her resin runs out.
chapters.value_shift: safe for now -> on a clock
beats: First light, nine days into the rains: Neela turns back on the warden's window ledge; the brazier-warmed cloth waits and Devan has the river pebble in his palm. She counts what is left in Ammu's pouch: two smears.
Society is shown at a cost: her page burned, her name went to Kodiyur on the closing writ by the last rider, and the crown hunts unvouched odiyans. The welt on his wrist answers her torn scar.
In the hall over Ittan's tally book she can read some marks in guild shorthand; a small sunbird beside certain lines means nothing to her yet.
They name their gap honestly: he needs the guild's contract for Asha as court evidence, she needs every page back in its owner's hands. They agree to go together and argue later.
At Ittan's grille Ittan asks only after his wife's medicine; Neela notes he is afraid of something that isn't Devan.
At dusk on the west rampart the langurs on the closed pass road go silent, which they do only when strangers walk it, and nobody can walk it in the rains.
chapters.reader_question_out: Who is on a road nobody can walk?
chapters.romance_change: Their first morning as true spouses becomes a working alliance with an honestly named conflict of goals.

chapters.title: The Justice at the Gate
chapters.goal: Keep Ittan alive to testify and keep Neela out of crown sight.
chapters.value_shift: master of his fort -> outranked inside it
beats: Dawn, Bhaskaran's horn: Justice Rema of the high court, 58, stands at the padippura with four escort in green sunbird sashes. They crossed by the goat path; their oilcloth packs are dry and their boots barely worn.

Rema presents the queen's warrant for Ittan, treason under the wartime charter. Devan says plainly he means to put Ittan before the court as witness to Asha's murder; Rema grants an assize hearing in three days.
The escort give numbers, not names. When the First Guard's cuff rides up, Devan sees a pale ridge on the inner wrist and reads it as a lamp-burn.
Rema remarks that her escort fixed the ropes on the crossing by night and that she never once saw them sleep.
Devan tells Neela everything before she asks; she points out that hiding her by day looks like guilt, so they agree she will be seen and say only true things.
Rema asks to meet the household witness who signed the closing writ, by name.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will Neela say to a crown justice who can hang her?
chapters.romance_change: He chooses full disclosure as protection instead of silent fences, and she accepts being told rather than shielded.

chapters.title: Numbers, Not Names
chapters.goal: Get through Rema's questions without a lie and learn who the escort are.
chapters.value_shift: unseen -> on a crown record in person
beats: Neela answers Rema in the hall as Kunjan Chirayil's ward; every sentence is true and she lets Rema infer the rest.
She asks the escort their names, as she asks everyone; they give only numbers, and it chills her more than the warrant.
The hounds run the yard loose again but whine and will not go near the escort's quarters.
Eravi salves her split nails; the salve smells of scorched tamarind and pine sap. She tells herself many barks smell bitter.
At night she finds Devan alone in the hall practising his case to an empty bench, badly. She coaches him: say less, say only what you can prove.
He asks what she would say if the court asked her what she is. She has no answer.
chapters.reader_question_out: What does the escort's silence hide, and what will Neela say under oath?
chapters.romance_change: She sees the formidable warden fail at speech and teaches him; for once she is the one who knows how to perform.

chapters.title: Ask Your Captain
chapters.goal: Get Ittan's sworn statement before the hearing.
chapters.value_shift: a witness in hand -> a witness silenced
beats: In the guardroom Ittan refuses to swear to anything and asks only that his wife's cough medicine be sent on; Devan promises it.
Devan offers to write to the widow's physicians himself; Ittan nearly breaks: 'Ask your captain what he brought me.' Then he falls silent.
Devan asks Muthu; Muthu laughs, then goes quiet, his lying tell. Devan says nothing yet because he needs Muthu at the gate through the hearing.
In the warden's chamber Neela suspects Muthu is the guild's man and Devan thinks he is the queen's; each argues the case.
They decide together not to give Rema the sunbird payment writ hidden behind the third slat, because the queen's justice cannot try the queen.
In the last dark hour Unni knocks: Rema has moved the execution to this dawn under a charter clause, and the escort are already in the court.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can Devan stop an execution without turning his garrison into mutineers?
chapters.romance_change: They make a joint decision to keep a secret from the crown, their first shared risk as equals under law.

chapters.title: Dawn Writ
chapters.goal: Help Devan delay the execution without exposing herself.
chapters.value_shift: the case has a witness -> the witness is dead
beats: In the courtyard in rain Devan enters a formal objection under assize law before the garrison; Rema rules the warrant outranks the hearing. He could stop it with sixty soldiers and chooses aloud not to make them traitors.
Ittan's last words are for his wife: keep the window open in rain. The escort carry out the sentence; Neela watches from the west rampart and looks at their hands, not the block.
On the wind from the escort she smells nightbark, faint and old, and the hounds whine. She guesses guild hunters carrying resin to take rogues, here for her.
At the kalari pit Devan cannot stop moving; Neela steps down and asks for a round. He spars with her by choice; she takes a point and lets him see her pleased.
At dusk the escort walk out into the rain toward the pass; the First Guard glances at Neela's split nails and says, 'It passes.'
Rema stays to hold assize until the pass opens, hearing the warden's case 'and any other the crown has sealed', and sets a second sealed writ case on the table.
chapters.reader_question_out: What is in the Justice's second sealed writ, and who were those guards?
chapters.romance_change: She asks to fight him rather than comfort him; he lets someone inside his guard, and competence becomes intimacy.

chapters.title: The Ledger He Needs
chapters.goal: Agree with Devan on what the ledger is for.
chapters.value_shift: shared plan -> shared plan with a fault line in it
beats: Devan writes to Ittan's widow and sends the medicine; Neela watches him do a kindness for the man who bought his death.
Rema tells Devan to bring the court paper the guild wrote, not his grief. The guild's contract books are ordinary ink and could be evidence; the pages are lives.
In the warden's chamber they fight honestly: he needs the ledger before the court; she says any court that holds it becomes a master. Both are right.
They settle a first term: contract books to the court, pages to their owners. Neither knows yet what the contract books hold.
She keeps the last smear of Ammu's resin rather than turn tonight; the ache is close.
She tells him she has to rob Chathu's groves before she can rob Chathu.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can a hunted rogue steal resin from the guild's own trees?
chapters.romance_change: Their first honest values fight ends in a stated term rather than a silence; disagreement survives respect.

chapters.title: Blackbark in the Rain
chapters.goal: Steal fresh resin and find where Chathu keeps the ledger.
chapters.value_shift: empty-handed -> armed with resin and a location
beats: Between downpours they ride the wood road by day. She taps a nightbark tree humming the tappers' song; the knife slips and the cut on her palm rises as a welt on his. He hands her a cloth without a word.
From a ridge they watch the Resin House: forty members training in the yards, hunters on the walls, Vellan limping on his lamed leg, Kirri's kennel roof below.
At dusk Chathu crosses to the shuttered well house with the black book under his arm and comes back without it.
On the way out the hunter Pachan finds them in daylight, sees Neela's face and lowers his hooked pole: 'I owe you a sweet.' He lets them go.
She rides home with a full flask; Ammu's pouch is empty for the first time, and she keeps it anyway.
The book is in the well house, and reaching it needs human hands at night, which she won't have.
chapters.reader_question_out: How do they reach the book when she can only get there as a leopard?
chapters.romance_change: They work as a team on her ground; his silent cloth after the shared cut shows he already counts her wounds as his.

chapters.title: Six Years of Letters
chapters.goal: Plan the raid and keep the fort steady under the Justice's eye.
chapters.value_shift: a trusted captain -> a captain named in front of the hall
beats: Devan and Bhaskaran draw the Resin House from Neela's counts and exits; Devan notices she will not draw the kennels.
She turns at dusk to scout the escort's trail toward the goat path; Devan holds Kannan's white pebble in his cheek all night, though nobody is watching him do it.
At dawn she reports she lost the trail in rain on the scree, and that something large went up it at night.
At supper Rema courteously thanks Captain Muthu, before the whole hall, for six years of faithful letters to the queen's household.
The hall goes quiet; Muthu's laugh does not come.
Muthu, white, says to Devan: 'Seventh day tomorrow. Give me a round.'
chapters.reader_question_out: What has Muthu been telling the queen, and what will he admit in the pit?
chapters.romance_change: He keeps the pebble through her first scouting night of the rains with no one to see it, a vow kept unwatched.

chapters.title: The Seventh Day
chapters.goal: Learn the truth from Muthu.
chapters.value_shift: suspicion -> a known traitor kept as captain
beats: At the dawn kalari Devan accepts the round; between blows Muthu confesses letters to the queen's household since the winter Asha died, asked of him 'to keep the warden safe'.
Muthu admits the grey packet he carried into Ittan's cell held a household order: say nothing and your wife is kept. He did not know an execution would follow.
Devan breaks the wax on the locked packet with Muthu beside him: every report confirmed, Neela's vow words included, nothing about the guild.
Muthu swears he never wrote to any guild and never told anyone Neela's cart order. Devan says 'I won't answer whether I believe that', takes the post-key and keeps him as captain.
That night Devan asks Neela how she would handle such a man, the first time he asks her about command. She says: give him a job he can't fake.
Devan names Muthu to hold Kettamala during the raid, with Rema inside its walls.
chapters.reader_question_out: If not Muthu, who in Kettamala talks to the guild?
chapters.romance_change: He asks her advice on command for the first time, letting her guard his back inside his own house.

chapters.title: Every Name in the Barracks
chapters.goal: Help hold the garrison while the fort whispers.
chapters.value_shift: a strange bride -> a woman the men can name back
beats: Barracks talk: the warden bowed to the crown and the bride is odd; Corporal Kandan says she has bewitched him.
Neela walks the barracks by day and learns every man's name and his mother's village, Asha's slate method; she wins Unni and Bhaskaran's lads but not Kandan.
In the kitchen she plays seven wells with Kannan and Chinna and cheats; Devan catches her and laughs, the first laugh since the execution.
At the foot of the west stair Janu says, 'You walk round it like I do.'
Neela hears the eleventh step ring hollow and sees the drain grate beneath it is newer iron than the stair.
She cannot say why her feet go wide of the parrot newel, and takes the long way up.
chapters.reader_question_out: Why does Neela's body avoid a stair she has no memory of?
chapters.romance_change: He watches her win his men with his dead sister's method, and his delight at her cheating returns laughter to their marriage.

chapters.title: Sharp-Edged Silver
chapters.goal: Finish the raid plan and decide who carries the book out.
chapters.value_shift: a plan -> a plan that puts every page in his hands for a night
beats: Rema pays Parukutty the harvest death-gift early in crown silver; Neela sees the sharp milled edge and the sprig, never handled, like the scouts' coin.
Devan weighs one coin against the scouts' satchel: the crown pays widows and raiders from the same mint run. He won't guess further aloud.
They work out the raid: she will be in shape, so he must climb the well shaft, and for a night he will hold every page.
He admits he is afraid of himself with that book; she admits she wants her own name more than she wants to be good.
Both restate the choice they have made twice: she is 27, he is 32, married by contract and again by vow.
She chooses to skip resin the night before the raid so she can be human with him, and the ache counts it against her.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will they promise each other before one of them holds forty lives?
chapters.romance_change: Mutual disclosure of what each fears in themselves around power moves them past trusting the other to admitting doubt in themselves.

chapters.title: The Bargain in the Dark
chapters.goal: Make a promise that protects each of them from the other's power.
chapters.value_shift: trust given -> trust with a check written into it
beats: In the warden's chamber the shutters are barred and her nails itch with the coming ache; she asks him to stay with her through dusk as a woman.
Explicit scene, open door: she leads, they check in with each other, and the pebble lies unused on the sill because she took no resin.
After, under the dark rule, they make the bargain: whoever holds the ledger, if they begin to read a page at night for any reason, the other takes it from their hand and they let go.
He asks for one of her eleven contracts, as she offered in book 1; she tells him the first, a port enforcer's man, plainly.
He chooses not to ask the second: 'After the book.'
She lies awake counting doors, knowing ten contracts remain to tell and not knowing which he will hate.
chapters.reader_question_out: Which of her ten untold contracts will break him?
chapters.romance_change: Intimacy becomes the place they write a mutual veto over each other's power, a new term in their marriage.

chapters.title: The Wood Road
chapters.goal: Get into position for the raid.
chapters.value_shift: watched in secret -> invited to watch
beats: They ride with eight of Bhaskaran's men in a break in the rain; Muthu holds Kettamala with Rema in it.
They plan the wound-share as a battle problem: any spear in her opens on him, so he must stay back with the lamp men and come in only for the shaft. He hates it and agrees.
At the dusk camp she smears resin and turns in front of him on purpose, the first turning he has been invited to see.
In shape she circles the camp while he talks quietly about Asha's parrots and Kannan's goat, because talk in the dark is safe between them now.
His old rib wound aches in the damp and she lies against his side until it eases.
She leaves the firelight for the Resin House wall, and he cannot follow until she calls.
chapters.reader_question_out: What waits inside the walls for a leopard alone?
chapters.romance_change: Her turning changes from something he witnessed by stealth to something she gives him to watch.

chapters.title: The Shuttered Well
chapters.goal: Clear the way to the book for Devan.
chapters.value_shift: unseen -> found
beats: In shape she enters by the drain path she and Ammu used as children; in the kennels Kirri lifts her head at Neela's scent and the anklet glints.
In the well house the iron box hangs on a chain in the shaft, padlocked; paws can't open it, so she gives the leopard's sawing call that signals Devan.
A hunter's lamp swings toward her; she knocks him down without killing him.
Pavi, 24, an otter on night watch, sees her and does not raise the alarm.
Vellan in bear shape comes round the cook-house corner on his lame leg, scenting the wind.
The bear finds her, and she is all that stands between it and the shaft Devan is climbing.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can she hold a bear off a man whose wounds are hers?
chapters.romance_change: She guards the shaft he is in, protecting him in her own domain while every blow she takes will land on him.

chapters.title: Bear and Lamp
chapters.goal: Get the book out and get Neela out alive.
chapters.value_shift: a raid -> a guild without a master
beats: In the shaft by lamplight Devan feels claw welts open across his back: Neela is fighting the bear above him.
He prises the box open with a pry bar and climbs into the yard with the black book.
Bhaskaran's men come in with lamps and spears as planned; the lamed bear faces light and blades and gives ground. Devan doesn't strike first; he strikes once, to the shoulder, when it rears over her.
On the cook-house step Chathu sees the book in Devan's hand and runs for the dark wood with Vellan and the hunters, knowing the members follow whoever holds it.
The forty, still in shape, gather at the yard's edge and do not attack; before first light they go into the tapping sheds to turn back unseen, as trained.
They come out dressed and look at the book; in front of all of them Devan hands it to Neela.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will Neela find when she opens it?
chapters.romance_change: He refuses mastery in public by handing her the book before forty witnesses, honouring their bargain before it is tested.

chapters.title: Lookout: Seventeen
chapters.goal: Find Asha's contract for Devan and read it honestly, as promised.
chapters.value_shift: a wife he trusts -> the lookout at his sister's death
beats: The forty bow when she takes the book, and she stands among them unable to tell whether she is their sister or their owner.
In Chathu's room by daylight she opens the contract quire; it is in guild cipher Devan can't read, so she reads aloud as promised.
Release is proven a lie: 'Kirri, released' is cross-referenced to kennel nine, and eleven more 'released' members lead to cages. Vellan's entries run several leaves and she turns past them.
Asha's contract: 'Kettamala, the warden's sister, the west stair. Buyer, the Keeper. Hand, Thirty. Lookout, Seventeen.' She reads every word and learns which fort at the same moment he does.
The parrot newel, the hollow eleventh step and her wide path round the stair all reread: she held the lamp at the foot of his sister's death.

The last quire is stitched in green thread under the queen's sunbird wax; Devan says leave it whole, an unbroken seal is evidence. He sets the contract book down carefully, says 'I need to walk', and goes into the rain without his cloak.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can their marriage survive a crime neither of them chose?
chapters.romance_change: The midpoint mirror recasts book 1's west stair and their whole first meeting: trust built becomes trust broken by a past neither chose.

chapters.title: The Broken Beak
chapters.goal: Decide what to do without lying to her or to the court.
chapters.value_shift: ease -> care without ease
beats: In the Resin House training yard in rain Devan runs the drill he uses to master his own hands.
He remembers the killing point he struck at 24 and the blow he struck the bear last night, and knows he could strike again.
He hears Asha's note: say it anyway. The contract he wanted for the court names his wife as party to the murder.
Neela comes out; she doesn't apologise for the guild, she asks what he needs. He says 'I won't answer that' to whether he can look at her, then 'I'm not leaving. I need a day.'
At dusk he puts the pebble in his cheek though she took no resin, and she sees it.
He sleeps across the master's-room door with his back to the wall; at dawn he asks for the second contract, and the third, wanting all eleven before he decides anything.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will he do once he knows all eleven?
chapters.romance_change: His care continues while his ease is gone; the withdrawal is honest, brief and disciplined, never punishment.

chapters.title: Forty Names
chapters.goal: Keep the forty safe, fed and guarded.
chapters.value_shift: a rogue -> a master in all but name
beats: She tells Devan the remaining contracts through the morning, flatly, then argues her belief: she was 21, blindfolded, holding a lamp; Chathu chose and Vellan struck, so it isn't hers. He says, 'I know. She's still dead.'
She learns every member's name; most know only numbers, and their intake rolls with their birth names are fastened to the pages in her hands.

Reasons to wait: rogues are hunted, Rema sits a day's ride away, Chathu has hunters in the wood, the groves need guarding. She decides to hold the pages 'until it's safe' and vouches for the forty as the House.
They obey her at once: groves guarded, kennels cleaned, Kirri washed. It is easy.
Before riding back to the fort Devan says gently that Chathu thought the ledger was mercy too. It lands.
Thilak, 41, brings her the master's tea and calls her 'Master' without irony; she doesn't correct him.
chapters.reader_question_out: How long can she hold forty lives before she becomes Chathu?
chapters.romance_change: A new strain enters: her first use of power is the thing he warned her about, and she rejects his warning.

chapters.title: Assize Weather
chapters.goal: Keep the garrison loyal and the court satisfied while his wife holds the guild.
chapters.value_shift: apart by choice -> riding to her before he's ready
beats: Rema asks where the warden rides; Devan answers truly but not fully, and she warns the court won't accept 'I won't answer that' for ever.
Kandan's faction refuses a patrol order; Devan answers in the yard, openly: 'If I'm wrong, the court will say so. Until then, walk.' He strikes no one and names the cost.
Muthu ran the fort honestly in his absence; Devan returns the post-key.
Eravi asks leave to ride up the wood road for medicines from 'a tapper I know'; Devan grants it absently.
At the assize table that night a shallow welt opens across Devan's ribs: Neela has been hurt at the House.
He rides at once, in the dark, alone.
chapters.reader_question_out: What has happened to Neela?

chapters.title: Nellimala
chapters.goal: Defend the groves and answer Chathu's offer.
chapters.value_shift: a number with no past -> a name and a village burned by agreement
beats: In the grove at dawn a hunter's arrow grazes her ribs; Devan arrives mud-soaked and cleans the wound. Neither speaks of Asha.
At the gate sits a tin of warm jaggery-sesame sweets; under them, her intake slip and Chathu's note: return the book and come home.
The slip: 'Indu, of Nellimala, coast side of the Monkey Pass. Village burned the second harvest. Sold at six years.' The goat path and the lantana make sense: she was born below Kettamala.

With the ledger's cipher key she reads Ittan's tally book properly at last: his extra passes, and sunbird-marked 'allowed' passes. 'Nellimala, second harvest' stands in the allowed column, twenty-one years back.
They understand together: the crown permits raids, and her village was burned by agreement.
She asks Devan to say her birth name aloud in daylight; he does. She says she will keep both names and tips the sweets into the fire.
chapters.reader_question_out: What can Devan prove now that the crown itself is in the tally book?
chapters.romance_change: The same crown wounded them both; for the first time since the midpoint they are injured parties together, and he gives her name back by daylight.

chapters.title: The Sunbird Column
chapters.goal: Rebuild the court case around what he can prove.
chapters.value_shift: a case built on grief -> a case built on evidence, his wife's name included
beats: Devan works out the pattern: the queen allows raids, Ittan sold extras on top, Asha found an extra and Ittan bought her death; when Devan asked for the seal registers, the queen bought his.
He can prove one conspiracy in Rema's court, Ittan's tokens and Asha's murder; the treaty and the queen's writ need the high court in full session.
He asks Neela to help him write the case in plain words; she asks him to help guard the groves with Bhaskaran's men. Each asks for help where they are weak.
He tells her his decision before acting: the contract goes to the court whole, lookout line included. He will not strike out her number.
She says she won't ask him to; she doesn't yet say she will stand beside it.
She asks to ride back to Kettamala with him, because there is someone she owes first.
chapters.reader_question_out: What does Neela owe, and to whom?
chapters.romance_change: Honesty replaces ease: he tells her his hardest decision before he acts, and she chooses not to bargain her way out of it.

chapters.title: The Hollow Step
chapters.goal: Ready herself to tell Janu.
chapters.value_shift: a gap in memory -> a memory she must speak
beats: She brings the ledger to Kettamala in her saddlebag and keeps it on her; Janu overfeeds her and she can't eat.
Eravi dresses her graze; his satchel reeks of nightbark. He asks how many members the House holds and on which day she will read their pages back. She answers neither and files the question.

Alone on the west stair at dusk without resin she counts forty-four steps and the eleventh rings. The memory comes: the blindfold lifted at the stair foot, a lamp in her hand, a parrot with a broken beak, a woman's voice above asking who was there.
She remembers holding the lamp steady because she was told to, and saying nothing.
Devan finds her there; he says he'll stand where she can see him and won't speak for her.
Janu passes with a lamp and stops ten paces from the stair foot as she always does; Neela calls her name.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will Janu do when she hears it?
chapters.romance_change: He offers presence without rescue: the right to watch her repair, not to do it for her.

chapters.title: Ten Paces
chapters.goal: Confess to Janu without excuse.
chapters.value_shift: not mine to answer for -> answering for it
beats: At the stair foot Neela tells Janu she held the lamp the night Asha died; she doesn't say 'the guild made me' until Janu asks why.
Janu strikes the newel, not Neela, then confesses her own guilt: she was asleep at the kitchen fire.
Janu asks one thing: was Asha afraid. Neela answers truthfully that Asha asked who was there, and that Neela, holding the light, did not answer.
Janu does not forgive her; she says 'Come and eat', because that is what Janu does.
Neela tells Devan the drain grate under the eleventh step is new iron; Gopan says the old postern under it was kept locked.
Gopan: 'Only the physician keeps that key.'
chapters.reader_question_out: Did the fort's own physician let Asha's killer in?
chapters.romance_change: Watching her confess without excuse is what lets Devan look at her again.

chapters.title: The Physician's Key
chapters.goal: Catch the inside informant.
chapters.value_shift: a fort with a hidden enemy -> the enemy named and the House exposed
beats: Devan waits at the drain postern at night; Eravi passes a salve jar through the grate to a runner from the pass village, who flees.

Eravi confesses: twenty years buying Resin House medicines for the fort and paying in news; six years ago he unlocked this postern for 'a guild man'; he passed on the cart order overheard outside the sickroom and the sword's position, and drained the stair lamps.
Tonight's jar told Chathu that Neela is at the fort, the House has no master in it, and the forty think she is just another one.
Devan apologises to Muthu in front of Bhaskaran, and Muthu takes it.
In the warden's chamber, second explicit scene: Devan says 'I choose you knowing'; she says 'Don't forgive me yet'; he says he won't, he'll choose. Forgiveness stops being the price of staying.
At first grey a rider comes off the wood road: the Resin House gate is shut against Bhaskaran's lads and Chathu's hunters are on the walls.
chapters.reader_question_out: What has Chathu done with the forty?
chapters.romance_change: Repair stops being a debt she pays; he names staying as his choice, not her reward, and the private declaration is made.

chapters.title: The Gate Shut
chapters.goal: Retake the House and the forty.
chapters.value_shift: a master -> a master deserted
beats: They ride the wood road; Devan leaves the assize table with Rema watching, and the court notes his absence.
At the Resin House the forty stand on the walls beside Chathu's hunters; Thilak shouts down: 'You kept the book. So did he. He says he'll burn ours.'
Chathu speaks gently at the gate: the groves for the book. Without resin the forty will ache, and so will she. He calls it a fair price.
She sees it plainly: the delay she called protection handed him the forty back.
Vellan, in human form at Chathu's shoulder, carves a small bird and watches her, not Devan.
Chathu tells her that at dusk he will force resin on the forty and send them into the wood; she can cage them with their pages or be hunted by them.
chapters.reader_question_out: Will she cage her sisters and brothers to survive the night?
chapters.romance_change: The cost of her choice lands on both, and she notices that he does not say he warned her; his restraint becomes a new reason to trust him.

chapters.title: Human at Dusk
chapters.goal: Keep Neela alive through the night.
chapters.value_shift: a couple with a plan -> two people and forty pages against a hunting wood
beats: On the slope above the House Neela has no resin; her flask is in the House stores with everyone's ration, so she will be human at night against forty animals.
She says it aloud: she has become Chathu. Devan doesn't argue; he says what she does next is still hers.
She tears Vellan's page from the ledger and gives it to Devan: if Vellan comes tonight, the choice belongs to the man with most right to it, and she trusts him not to read it.
At dusk the forced turnings begin in the yard; the cries carry, and Devan names it for the cruelty it is.
He takes the lamp and the ledger onto his own pack so she can run.
Forty animals pour out of the gate into the wood, and every bite on her will open on him.
chapters.reader_question_out: Will either of them read a page before dawn?
chapters.romance_change: She hands him the leash of his sister's killer and trusts him with the choice, the most costly trust she has ever given.

chapters.title: Before Dawn
chapters.goal: Survive the night without caging anyone.
chapters.value_shift: hunted by her own -> the hunt broken without a single caging
beats: Forced-turned members hunt them through the wood; she holds forty pages and a lamp and reads none. Devan carries her when she falls, and both bleed from the same bites.
When she calls members by their names, not their numbers, some break off.
Near dawn Vellan in bear shape brings her down at the blackbark tree where Ammu died; Devan stands over them with Vellan's page open and the lamp lit. One sentence would cage his sister's killer.
She keeps the bargain: she reaches up and takes the page from his hand, and he lets go.
Instead she reads Vellan a line from the contract book, ordinary ink and no page: 'Thirty. Release not to be granted. Sell to the crown when spent.' The bear stops.
At first light Vellan turns back in front of them, so Devan becomes his witness against his will; the members slink back to the House sheds to turn unseen.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will she do with forty pages now that the night is over?
chapters.romance_change: The bargain made in bed holds under the heaviest pressure: she stops him and he lets her, proving the check works both ways.

chapters.title: Daylight Reading
chapters.goal: Make herself no one's master.
chapters.value_shift: holder of the ledger -> holder of nothing but her own name
beats: Muthu rides in with thirty of the garrison, against Rema's written order that no soldier aid a rogue, and burns his unsent report in the gate fire; Chathu's hunters lay down their poles and Pachan opens the gate.
In the yard by daylight Neela first tells the forty the cost, that every listener becomes their witness, and asks them to choose; then she reads every page aloud in full, Vellan's too.
Each member takes their own page; some keep their intake rolls and hear their birth names for the first time; Thilak burns his, and his village with it.
At kennel nine she reads Kirri's page and lays it in the straw by the anklet; Kirri stays a civet, and that stays lost.
Devan holds no page now, only a witness's word; he gives Vellan his back and lets him go, and Vellan walks into the wood.

Chathu, with an empty ledger, is bound for the Justice; Pachan stays to keep the kennels and groves; the forty ride with one season's flasks; Neela keeps only the sealed green quire and the contract books for Devan's court.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will the court do with a confessed lookout and an emptied guild?
chapters.romance_change: Recognition: each watches the other refuse power they could have kept, and he watches her free the man who killed his sister.

chapters.title: The Assize
chapters.goal: Prove one conspiracy before the court.
chapters.value_shift: a sister's death unexplained -> a sister's death on record
beats: In Kettamala hall Rema sits; Devan lays out Asha's token, the scouts' tally, Ittan's blanks and tally book, and the guild contract.
Chathu, bound, testifies in debts and balances: the Keeper bought the warden's sister.
Neela stands unasked and reads the lookout line herself, under her name and her number; Devan did not ask her to.
Rema records the finding for the high court: Asha's murder and the pass sales were one conspiracy, bought by the Keeper. Asha's name goes into the record.
Devan says he holds one more document, for the high court in full session only; Rema notes it and does not press.
Rema asks the household witness, under oath, whether she is an odiyan. Neela says yes.
chapters.reader_question_out: What does the queen's sealed writ say about a warden who harbours one?
chapters.romance_change: He wins his goal with her as a witness against herself, and sees she chose the stand he would have spared her.

chapters.title: The Sealed Writ
chapters.goal: Keep Devan his fort, if she can.
chapters.value_shift: a warden's wife -> the reason he is no longer warden
beats: Rema opens the second sealed case: the queen's writ, dated before the execution, says that if the warden harbours an unvouched odiyan he is stripped of Kettamala and office and leaves within three days; Captain Muthu holds the seal in trust.
Before the hall Neela offers to leave alone so he can keep the fort; Devan refuses aloud, his choice, public: his declaration.
She answers with her own declaration in front of everyone.
Devan unhooks the iron warden's seal and puts it in Muthu's hand: hold the pass for the villages. Muthu swears to the border, not to the household.
Kandan, who called her a witch, is the first to salute Devan as he walks out.
In private Rema tells them the queen does nothing by accident and will remember where they go.
chapters.reader_question_out: Where can a stripped warden and a confessed odiyan go in a closed country?
chapters.romance_change: Public declaration under real loss: love chosen at the price of his office, before his men.

chapters.title: The Third Slat
chapters.goal: Leave Kettamala with nothing left unsaid.
chapters.value_shift: warden and bride -> partners
beats: On the last night he takes the chit, the sunbird writ and the gift seal from the hollow behind the third slat; the slat creaks as it always has. He never fixed it.
Janu packs food and at last finishes her leopard story with the ending she never told: the leopard comes home.
Third explicit scene: the shutters open to the rain on purpose and she took no resin, by choice. New terms: no warden and no bride, partners who lead together, each at the other's back.
Afterwards she lets him count her breathing for once, and he finds she has a hitch too.
At dawn he wakes to her counting his.
Forty riders wait below the padippura in the rain.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will the green-sealed quire tell them once there is no court left to keep it for?
chapters.romance_change: Without the fort they make the bargain of equals; the room that once hid her is opened.

chapters.title: Sold to the Crown
chapters.goal: Lead the forty to safety in the hills.
chapters.value_shift: homeless and hunted -> homeless, hunted and free, with a bigger enemy named
beats: They ride into the hills with forty who each hold their own page, to a pepper hunters' shelter above the tree line.
They have one season's flasks, tapping knives and a grove map; the ache waits for all of them.
At dusk Neela and Devan break the queen's green seal on the last quire: a list headed 'Sold to the crown', thirty numbers, every page cut out.
The langurs below go silent; Vellan walks into the firelight as a man, without resin, while the others turn.
Vellan confirms it: the queen's own guard are odiyans; the escort who crossed the closed pass were among them, and their pages sit in her crown leaf.
Neela says 'Indu' to herself, then 'Neela'; Devan says they will need a bigger hall. Thirty more pages are held by the one master they cannot reach.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can they free the queen's own night-guard, and what will it cost Varanad?
chapters.romance_change: HFN: homeless and hunted, they choose a shared purpose larger than either of them, a partnership sworn in the open.

clues.clue: Langurs go silent on the closed pass road at dusk
Ammu's pouch holds two smears of resin
The First Guard's inner wrist shows a pale ridge Devan reads as a lamp-burn
The hounds whine and won't go near the escort's quarters
Eravi's salve smells of nightbark
Ittan: 'Ask your captain what he brought me.'
Rema's second sealed writ case
Nightbark on the wind from the escort at the execution
Chathu takes the black book to the shuttered well house at dusk
Pachan: 'I owe you a sweet.'
Muthu swears he never told the guild the cart order
Janu: 'You walk round it like I do.'
The drain grate under the eleventh step is newer iron
Crown death-gift silver has the scouts' sharp milled edge
Eleven contracts told one at a time; he asks only the first
The green-sealed last quire is left whole as evidence
Vellan's ledger entries, which Neela turns past
Eravi asks leave to ride the wood road for medicines
Ittan's tally book in guild shorthand with sunbird marks
The First Guard's 'It passes' to Neela
Devan withholds the sunbird payment writ for the full high court
The forty ride with one season's resin; the groves stay behind
